title: The One on the Top Shelf
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：bird　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bird 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my grandfather was shown ① a bird that had been dead for nine years, and he said the showing was the whole of the lesson. The ② bird, meaning the creature and not the specimen, had been shot in March and named in June; a bird, he said, is the only animal that is easier to love once it has stopped moving.

Every ③ bird in that collection was labelled in the same hand, and the ④ bird on the top shelf, meaning the one he had found himself and not either of those, was the only one he ever described. A bird, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part a name you can spell; my grandfather said the patience is the part nobody sees.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ bird was the whole of the morning, meaning the singing and not the creature. The ⑥ bird, meaning the noise before six and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody hears and nobody gets up for; a bird, she said, is either something in a case or the only word that means both an animal and a morning. He said the morning came first.

By 1966 the ⑦ bird had become a photograph in a book, and the book had become an argument about whether it was rare. The ⑧ bird of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in April, was nine years of dust and one found specimen; a bird, he said, is either the thing on the top shelf or the reason you learned to be quiet. She said the quiet was the part that mattered.

The ⑨ bird I remember is the one on the top shelf, which was given away in 1969 and was never replaced. A ⑩ bird, my mother said in 1971, is the only creature that improves by being described; every bird, she said, is a morning that has agreed to look like an animal. He said the morning was the real part.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 鸟（指那只动物，与标本相对）
C. 固定搭配：be shown a bird 被给看一只鸟
D. n. 鸟（指那批收藏里每一只）
E. n. 鸟（指顶层架子上那一）
F. n. 鸟鸣（指清晨的叫声）
G. n. 鸟鸣（抽象：那种声音）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bird that had been dead for nine years
The bird, meaning the creature and not the specimen
the bird on the top shelf
bird was the whole of the morning
The bird, meaning the noise before six
the bird had become a photograph in a book
The bird of the whole thing
A bird, my mother said in 1971

answers.why: be shown a bird 意为“被给看一只鸟”，1947 年有人给祖父看一只已经死了九年的鸟。
bird 意为“鸟”，指那只动物而不是标本，它三月被打下来，六月被命名。
bird 指那批收藏里每一只鸟，每一只都是同一笔迹贴的标签。
bird 指顶层架子上那一（他自己找到的那一只），是唯一他描述过的。
bird 意为“鸟鸣”，指清晨的叫声，母亲说 bird 就是那个早晨的全部。
bird 为抽象用法，指那种声音，是屋里人人都听见、却没人愿意起床去看的东西。
bird 意为“鸟”，到 1966 年这个 bird 成了书里的一张照片。
bird 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖父四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九年的灰尘和一只自己找到的标本。
bird 意为“鸟”，我记得的是顶层架子上那一，1969 年被送掉，再没补上。
bird 为抽象总称，母亲说鸟是唯一会因为被描述而变好的生物。
